entities.summary: Ben Shalom Bernanke is an American economist who served as the 14th chairman of the Federal Reserve from 2006 to 2014. After leaving the Federal Reserve, he was appointed a distinguished fellow at the Brookings Institution. During his tenure as chairman, Bernanke oversaw the Federal Reserve's response to the 2008 financial crisis, for which he was named the 2009 Time Person of the Year. Before becoming Federal Reserve chairman, Bernanke was a tenured professor at Princeton University and chaired the Department of Economics there from 1996 to September 2002, when he went on public service leave.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As chairman of the Federal Reserve during the 2008 financial crisis, Ben Bernanke implemented unconventional monetary policies that averted a global depression, stabilizing the US economy and averting widespread unemployment. His actions had significant regional impact on the global economic landscape.
